questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

The first prize will be won by Williams in the singing competition.

options.text: Williams will win the first prize in the singing competition.
Williams will be winning the first prize in the singing competition.
Williams had won the first prize in the singing competition.
Williams wins the first prize in the singing competition.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Williams will win the first prize in the singing competition.**'

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence is in passive voice, indicated by the structure "**will be won by**" followed by the subject "**Williams**".
 
• To convert to **active voice**, the **subject **(**Williams**) should be the doer of the action and placed at the beginning of the sentence.
 
• The verb "**will win**" properly corresponds to "**will be won**" in active voice, keeping the **future tense intact**.
 
• The sentence structure for active voice should clearly indicate that Williams is the one performing the action (winning) without changing the tense or the meaning of the original sentence.
 
• Hence, the correct sentence in active voice is '**Williams will win the first prize in the singing competition.**'

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2**: Uses "will be winning" which suggests a future continuous tense, altering the simplicity and directness of the prediction found in the original sentence.
 
• **Option 3**: Incorrectly changes the tense to past perfect ("had won"), which does not match the future intention of the original sentence.
 
• **Option 4**: Uses the present simple tense ("wins"), which does not convey the future aspect of the event as clearly as the correct option.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The Thar desert is _________ in the state of Rajasthan.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**situated**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Thar Desert is a large arid region in the northwestern part of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• It is primarily located in the Indian state of Rajasthan, covering a significant portion of the area.
 
• The use of the term "**situated**" is appropriate because it accurately describes the location or positioning of the Thar Desert within a geographical context. (स्थित)
 
• Other options, such as "**bounded**," "**seen**," or "**placed**" do not appropriately capture the natural placement or geographical setting of the Thar Desert.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

 

**Complete Sentence**: *The Thar Desert is **situated__ **in the state of Rajasthan*.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Bounded**: Suggests limits or boundaries that are not the primary context of the question. The desert does demarcate regions, but the term itself does not focus on the location. (घिरा)
 
• **Seen**: It implies the ability to visually perceive, which is not relevant to indicating the geographical setting of the Thar Desert. (देखा)
 
• **Placed**: This implies an action or the act of positioning something in a specific location that does not naturally align with the manner in which geographical features are described. (रखा)

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

A piece of information received __by word of mouth__ has no authenticity.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**in spoken form**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "**by word of mouth**" refers to information that is passed from one person to another through verbal communication rather than in writing. It suggests a less formal, and potentially less reliable, method of communication. (शब्दों के माध्यम से)

 
 
• **Example**: The local bakery gained popularity mostly **by word of mouth**; they did very little advertising.
 
 
 
• The correct interpretation of this idiom, "**in spoken form**", relates to anything conveyed through speech rather than through written documentation. (मौखिक रूप से)
 
 
• **Example**: The instructions for the game were given **in spoken form**, which led to some confusion among the participants.
 
 
 
• Hence, the correct answer is in **spoken form**.

Therefore, the correct answer is “**Option 4**”.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Through an official order**: This means to carry out or execute something based on a command or instruction given by a higher authority. (आधिकारिक आदेश के माध्यम से)

 
 
• **Example**: The new policy was implemented **through an official order** from the government.
 
 
 
• **Through rumours**: This refers to information that is spread by people talking to each other, often not based on fact. (अफवाहों के जरिए)
 
 
• **Example**: The news of the celebrity's visit spread **through rumours** long before it was officially confirmed.
 
 
 
• **In written form**: This means information that is provided in writing, as opposed to being spoken or conveyed verbally. (लिखित रूप में)
 
 
• **Example**: The contract outlined all the terms and conditions **in written form** to avoid any misunderstanding.

• Other options do not accurately reflect the process of internalizing or learning information presented by someone, making "**understood**" the most fitting selection.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 4**'.

The propaganda was made to invade ________ neighbouring countries.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**smaller**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Propaganda is often utilized as a tool to justify actions against other entities, typically portraying the targets in a way that supports the agenda of the propagandist.
 
• In the context of invasion, the selection of "**smaller**" neighbouring countries implies a strategic choice, often motivated by the perception of easier conquest or lesser resistance due to size, resources, or military strength.
 
• The use of "**smaller**" aligns with historical and contemporary instances where larger, more powerful nations target less powerful neighbours for various strategic gains.
 
• Other options do not fit the typical strategic rationale behind the use of propaganda in the context of invasions, as they suggest criteria (size, unfamiliarity, or strength) that don't inherently justify the choice of target in the same way.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

 

**Complete Sentence**: *The propaganda was made to invade **smaller**__ neighbouring countries.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Largest**: Suggests targeting the biggest countries, which is less common due to the higher risks and challenges involved.
 
• **Stranger**: Implies targeting countries that are unfamiliar or unknown, which is not a typical criterion for invasion as familiarity with the target is important for strategic planning.
 
• **Strongest**: Indicates targeting the most powerful countries, which contradicts the usual strategic considerations of choosing more manageable targets for invasion.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**the**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The definite article '**the**' is used before singular or plural nouns when the noun is specific.
 
• In this case, "**the white coat**" refers to the specific white coat of the white tiger.
 
• The use of '**the**' emphasizes that we are talking about a particular white coat that is characteristic of the white tiger. It is not just any white coat, but the distinct coat that has beautiful black stripes on it.
 
• The context requires a definite article because it specifies the white coat of the white tiger, which is already a particular subject being discussed in the passage.
 
• Using '**a**', '**an**', or '**of**' would not correctly specify the white coat being referred to in this context.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

 

**Complete Passage**: *The white tiger is an offspring of Bengal tiger, which has the necessary gene for white colouring. It has beautiful black stripes on **the__** white coat. (2) ______ species of animal has blue eyes and a pink nose.*

*A pure white tiger is totally white without any stripes, which is due to the presence of double recessive allele in the genetic code. It happens only in the Bengal tiger subspecies, and only one in 10,000 births can have it naturally. White tigers are rarely seen in the wild, and only twelve of them have been spotted in India (3) ______ the last one-hundred years. Tigers have a lifespan of 10-15 years. They are (4) _______ animals, and are fond of hunting at night. Their diet consists of any animals that they can catch, and can eat up to 40 pounds of meat at one time. After such a big meal, they usually remain away for several days from food. They are slow runners, (5) ______ good swimmers. They are poor climbers and cannot climb a tree easily. They live in an area ranging from 10 to 30 square miles depending upon the availability of prey, water and shelter. Habitat loss, poaching and expansion of the human population have together contributed to their becoming endangered. They are widely hunted for their body-parts, which are used in traditional Chinese medicines.*

• **Option 1)** 'a' is an indefinite article used before nouns that begin with a consonant sound. It is used when referring to a general example of something, which doesn't apply in this specific context.
 
• **Option 2) **'an' is an indefinite article used before nouns that begin with a vowel sound. It is also used for general examples, not specific ones like in this case.
 
• **Option 4)** 'of' is a preposition that is used to indicate relationships between nouns, such as belonging or origin. It would not fit grammatically or contextually in the blank space.
